text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- The Norwegian Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission may withdraw brokerhouse Platou Securities' right to manage share issues after Platou administrered a share issue in Norwegian Applied Technology (NAT), a small offshore company that became listed on the Oslo Bourse last month. Several portfolio managers in insurance companies were given the opportunity to buy stock while many other investors were shut out from the issue.
- Parliament discusses terms for NATO's expansion into Eastern Europe.
- The ruling Labour Party, which faces elections in September, slips in the latest opinion poll to 32.1 percent from 33.8 percent in January.
- Union Bank of Norway said on Thursday higher costs and lower interest margins led to a 21 percent drop in 1996 net profits, but the bank was pleased with the result.

- Norway's largest shipping company Bergesen ASA posted 1996 profits far exceeding expectations, but attributed the performance to a change in accounting principles. Managing director Morten Bergesen says income is too low but that solidity is robust.
- Forestry company Norske Skogindustrier ASA saw 1996 profits drop. The paper sector did well but pulp did poorly.

- Riulf Rustad, investment executive in Norway's biggest insurance company, Storebrand ASA, quit because he was fed up with the press. Media had questioned his role in a controversy over alleged trading by portfolio managers for personal gain.
- The government wants to slap Value Added Tax on Internet subscriptions, advertisment and commercial home pages.
